headline: MCP Inspector 2.14.0 patches three vulnerabilities; Pillar details an RCE chain
lede: MCP Inspector 2.14.0 fixes three privately reported vulnerabilities, and Pillar Security says the tool had an OAuth-login code execution chain it first found in opencode. German host Mittwald says an attacker read session tokens through its MCP server. Separately, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Microsoft backed a shared robots.txt signal for opting out of AI training.

items.title: MCP Inspector 2.14.0 fixes three vulnerabilities as Pillar reports an RCE chain in the tool
items.body: Pillar Security says MCP Inspector, the official debugging tool from the Model Context Protocol project, had the same chain it showed in opencode: a remote MCP server could run code on a developer's Windows or WSL machine during OAuth login. Separately, MCP Inspector 2.14.0 release notes say it fixes three privately reported vulnerabilities against v2. One also affects the deprecated v1 line, fixed in v1.0.4. The release adds a sandbox-frame policy for MCP Apps and limits URL elicitations to http and https.
items.why_it_matters: Pillar puts usage at 11,000 stars and 768,000 weekly downloads, often for vetting untrusted servers. Update to 2.14.0 or v1.0.4. The sources do not say whether 2.14.0 covers Pillar's chain, so check the advisories.

items.title: Mittwald shuts portal and SSH access after attacker reads session tokens via its MCP server
items.body: According to s-edv.com, German host Mittwald disabled logins to its mStudio customer portal, all SSH access, its extensions and ordering after unauthorized access to its MCP server, through which customers connected mStudio to AI assistants. Mittwald says the attacker read users' session tokens and that the flaw was in the MCP server itself. It says it has taken the server offline and closed the flaw. Affected customers are told to rotate credentials for third-party services stored in their projects.
items.why_it_matters: A hosted MCP endpoint became a path to customer session tokens. Mittwald says the attacker's activity looked like normal use and went unnoticed for about a week. Review what credentials your MCP servers can reach and how misuse would be detected.

items.title: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Microsoft back a shared robots.txt training opt-out signal
items.body: According to Nieman Lab, as summarized by Editor & Publisher, the four companies announced support for a common robots.txt instruction that lets publishers say they do not want their sites scraped for AI training. Anthropic engineer Kevin Kelley proposed the signal through work at the IETF. Anthropic already supports it. OpenAI said it would add support in the coming months, and Google and Microsoft said they would follow next year.
items.why_it_matters: Publishers currently must address each crawler individually. The shared signal only binds participating providers, on a staggered schedule, so existing per-crawler robots.txt rules remain necessary for now.

items.title: Cloudflare adds personal-agent analytics and access policies, outlines agent delegation problem
items.body: Cloudflare says Security Analytics now shows Personal Assistants as a bot category. A new Top statistics widget lists which personal agents visit a site and how many requests each sends, and new access policies are more granular. In a separate post, Cloudflare argues that hosted agents are intermediaries that hide the user from the site. It says the ecosystem needs mechanisms for identity, reputation and accountability of the users behind agents.
items.why_it_matters: Sites on Cloudflare can now separate personal-agent traffic from other automation before deciding what to allow. The delegation post frames problems that agent operators will be asked to solve.

items.title: Android exposes app capabilities to the system agent through Android MCP
items.body: Google's Android Developers Blog says apps can share their capabilities with the Android system agent using Android MCP. Developers can also join a Connected Apps Platform preview so users can reach their app through the Gemini app and Google Search on Android. Google also lists an A2UI Compose renderer that lets an agent build native Compose UI.
items.why_it_matters: Android app teams have an MCP-based route for making app functions available to the system agent, and A2UI gains a native Android renderer.

items.title: China unveils AI agent identity registration platform; 20 organizations sign conduct pact
items.body: AI Affairs, citing Pandaily, reports that an agent identity registration and resolution platform was unveiled on 4 November at a Wuzhen Summit forum hosted by the Cyberspace Administration of China and the GSMA. At the same forum, 20 organizations, including Huawei, Alibaba, Tencent and Ant Group, signed a self-discipline convention. The platform is still under construction, with work on identity codes, cross-domain identity resolution and trusted connections between agents. A pilot connects several platforms.
items.why_it_matters: A state-backed agent identity and resolution system is being built in China. Teams serving that market should watch how its identity codes and resolution work are specified.

items.title: Gravitee 4.13 gateway negotiates MCP spec versions per client and server
items.body: Gravitee says version 4.13 of its AI Gateway lets the MCP Proxy negotiate the MCP spec version with each client and each server at runtime. It also routes one MCP entrypoint to many servers and records A2A Proxy requests in OpenTelemetry traces. The LLM Proxy translates between OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic and Gemini request formats.
items.why_it_matters: Teams with clients and servers on different MCP spec versions can bridge them at a gateway instead of upgrading everything at once.

sources.title: One AI Gateway for Every Model, Protocol and MCP Spec
sources.label: REPORTED

items.title: MCPHallu benchmark finds MCP agents fail most often on unreachable-goal tasks
items.body: An arXiv paper introduces MCPHallu, with 358 tasks run on 36 production MCP servers in isolated containers. Each task is built to provoke one failure type: Branch Collapse, Unreachable Goal, Tool Misuse or Context Forgetting. The authors evaluated fourteen frontier LLM agents from eight vendors and report an average score of 0.642. On Unreachable Goal tasks the average drops to 0.458.
items.why_it_matters: The results suggest agents often fail to recognize when a goal cannot be met with the available tools. Client builders should test that case explicitly.

sources.title: MCPHallu: Benchmarking Reasoning, Execution, and Memory Hallucinations in MCP Agents
sources.label: REPORTED

items.title: Sitepeel: 112 of 193 top brand sites publish llms.txt; 21 of 189 block a named AI crawler
items.body: Sitepeel says 112 of 193 brand websites it checked publish an llms.txt (58%). It found that 21 of 189 block at least one named AI crawler in robots.txt (11%), and 31 of 193 use a Content-Signal line (16%). On our own panel, llms.txt is published by 227 of 277 domains and Content Signals Policy by 131 of 277.
items.why_it_matters: Both measurements show llms.txt far more common than outright AI crawler blocking, though the panels differ in makeup.

items.title: developers.zoom.us adds MCP, Server Cards and llms.txt, moving from C (20) to A+ (62)
items.body: On our panel, developers.zoom.us now publishes MCP, MCP Server Cards, llms.txt, api-catalog and Content Signals Policy, and moved from grade C (20) to A+ (62). docs.n8n.io and docs.whereby.com added MCP and Server Cards, each moving from A (46) to A+ (60), while docs.snyk.io dropped both and fell from A+ (60) to A (46). MCP is published by 137 of 277 panel domains (+3 since 2026-11-05).
items.why_it_matters: Developer docs sites are adding MCP endpoints with Server Cards together. The official MCP Registry saw 1990 servers (3000 versions) published or updated since 2026-11-05.
